finding_text: Parity test (test_us0120_closure_command_file_parity) asserts byte-identity only at pytest-run time. A developer editing .cursor/commands/closure.md without updating template/.cursor/commands/closure.md will cause silent drift between deliveries; no continuous guard (git hook or pre-commit) enforces ongoing byte-identity. Additionally, each /closure execution mandates an append to docs/engineering/state.md (per closure.md §Phase responsibility), yet enforce-triad-hot-surface.py already reports STATE_ARCHIVE_REQUIRED (exit 1, 1447/1000 lines). Every future /closure run amplifies this pre-existing hot-surface violation without triggering archival; the execute-phase acceptance of this as 'pre-existing' defers the accumulation without bounding it.

The /closure mutation ordering contract (backlog.md → acceptance.md → state.md → closure-verification.md per DEC-0040 §Artifact ordering) is enforced by prose in closure.md only. validate_closure_verification.py validates the closure-verification.md output schema but does not verify mutation sequencing; a conforming closure run that writes state.md before backlog.md passes all 10 contract tests undetected. Separately, test_us0120_auto_phase_plan_includes_closure (marker 6) accepts the OR fallback condition '`closure`' appearing anywhere in auto.md — it does not assert that closure is positioned BETWEEN release and refresh-context in the phase plan arrays, leaving the ordering invariant of DEC-0082's ship macro unverified by test.

CLOSURE_LEGACY_DRIFT reason code and its 3-signal drain-hook detection exist to handle in-flight stories at the US-0120 ship boundary; no sunset criterion is defined (e.g., 'retire once all pre-US-0120 release_queue rows with status=released are confirmed DONE'). This logic will persist as perpetual dead code after the transition backlog drains, creating ongoing maintenance surface. Additionally, test_us0120_backward_compat_drain_hook (marker 10) validates only that 'CLOSURE_LEGACY_DRIFT' and 'status=released' appear as substrings in closure.md — it does not execute the 3-signal detection logic or simulate a drain-hook scenario, so the actual backward-compat runtime behavior is untested beyond text presence.

D5 (install/upgrade/clean) and AC-3 lock removal of `.opencode/` only when `--host` includes opencode, but do not name fail-closed behavior when an operator runs `clean --host cursor` after a prior `--host both` install: orphaned `.opencode/` can persist with no documented reason code or AC-7 contract-test obligation. Separately, D1 names `INSTALL_HOST_INVALID` for unknown `--host` values but omits input-boundary rules for case folding (`OpenCode` vs `opencode`) and whitespace trimming across the triple installers (D6) — divergent PS/Bash/Python parsing is a realistic failure mode before execute.

D6/D7 couple `installer-owned-paths.manifest`, triple-installer copy engines, and `check_intake_template_parity.py --scope=opencode-adapter`, yet discovery Q7 (manifest host-row encoding) and Q8 (kernel vs host pack gating) remain open: there is no explicit interface contract stating which manifest rows are always-installed kernel paths (`docs/`, `scripts/`, `its_magic/`, …) versus host-gated `.cursor/` / `.opencode/` surfaces. Vision discovery notes assume kernel paths stay host-agnostic, but without a locked encoding the three installers can diverge on copy-filter semantics before `/architecture` authors the US-0121 section.

D3 and AC-1 permit `agents/`, `commands/`, `plugins/` or a 'documented equivalent' before discovery Q6 resolves the minimum empty-but-valid layout (placeholder files vs empty dirs vs repo-root `opencode.json`) — premature generalization that invites execute-time layout debates. Discovery Q9 (active repo-root `.opencode/` mirror for dogfooding) is YAGNI for this slice: D3 already satisfies delivery via `template/.opencode/` only; no AC requires an active mirror, so carrying Q9 as a discovery open question adds optional scope surface unrelated to the ten unchecked ACs.

R-0109 Q12 locks host-scoped `clean` orphan behavior (`OPENCODE_ORPHANED_BY_CLEAN_CURSOR` when `clean --host cursor` follows `--host both`) but does not define `upgrade`/`missing` when `--host` shrinks between runs (e.g. prior `both` install then `upgrade --host cursor`): `.opencode/` may remain stale while kernel and `.cursor/` paths refresh. D5/AC-3 gate OpenCode copy on the current `--host` but name no diagnostic reason code, operator guidance, or AC-7 contract-test obligation for host-downgrade staleness. Q12 normalize-then-validate also omits duplicate/conflicting `--host` argv (last-wins vs fail-closed) across `bin/its-magic.js` and triple-installer wrappers.

Q7 locks parallel `[opencode_install_include_paths]` / `[opencode_clean_paths]` sections and Q8 states `--host` gates only `.cursor/` and `.opencode/`, but the existing `[install_include_paths]` still mixes kernel rows (`docs/`, `scripts/`, `its_magic/`, …) with `.cursor/**` in one section. R-0109 does not lock the parser predicate that suppresses `.cursor/` copies when `--host opencode` while still installing kernel rows from the same section — only additive opencode sections are specified. Without an explicit mixed-section skip contract (prefix filter vs host-tagged rows), PowerShell/Bash/Python installers can diverge on whether `.cursor/` is copied, skipped, or partially upgraded before `/architecture` authors the US-0121 interface.

Q10 locks `template/.opencode/.gitignore` with four pattern groups including defense-in-depth `auth.json` (lives outside the repo per OpenCode docs) and speculative `*.local.json{,c}` under `.opencode/` before US-0122/US-0123 define any such filenames in the pack. D8/AC-10 require secrets and vendor-slug protection, not preemptive globs for files this slice never ships. `/architecture` should default to `.env` / `.env.*` plus `.opencode/opencode.json{,c}` only and defer extra patterns until a later slice names a concrete local-only artifact — otherwise parity tests must maintain ignore rules for hypothetical files.

Host-scoped mode table (`docs/engineering/architecture.md` `# US-0121` §Host-scoped missing / upgrade / clean; `decisions/DEC-0120.md` §5) names `OPENCODE_STALE_BY_UPGRADE_CURSOR` and `OPENCODE_ORPHANED_BY_CLEAN_CURSOR` when shrinking from `--host both`, but `missing --host cursor` after a prior `--host both` install only skips `.opencode/` rows with no named diagnostic for a leftover `.opencode/` tree — asymmetric with upgrade/clean and undetected by markers 8–9. Separately, compose claims US-0008 `overwrite` semantics UNCHANGED yet host scoping is locked only for missing/upgrade/clean: no row defines `overwrite --host opencode|both` behavior for `.cursor/`, kernel rows, or stale diagnostics (AC-3 names only missing/upgrade/clean).

Without a locked pair manifest (e.g. manifest sections only vs future active mirror), parity scope and triple-installer copy semantics can diverge at execute.
